client: I've been feeling really overwhelmed with anxiety about my presentation at the annual conference next week. Yesterday, during practice, I completely forgot my lines, and it just made everything feel worse. I'm starting to doubt whether I can actually pull this off, and I’m not sure if therapy can really help me with this kind of pressure.
therapist: It sounds like you're feeling a deep sense of anxiety and overwhelm about your upcoming presentation, especially after a challenging practice session. It's completely understandable to doubt yourself in such a high-pressure situation, but remember that many people experience similar feelings, and therapy can provide strategies to help manage that pressure. Let's explore some of those thoughts together and find ways to build your confidence for the conference.
vocal_descriptors: very high pitch, soft-spoken, moderate-paced speech

client: I really appreciate you saying that, but it's hard for me to shake off this anxiety. I keep thinking about how everyone will be watching me and judging every mistake I make. It feels like no matter what I do, I won't be able to meet their expectations, and that just makes it worse.
therapist: I can sense how deeply this anxiety is affecting you, especially with the fear of being judged by others. It’s natural to worry about meeting expectations, but it might help to remember that everyone makes mistakes, and most people are more focused on their own experiences than on critiquing yours. Let’s work on reframing those thoughts and finding ways to ease some of that pressure as the presentation approaches.
vocal_descriptors: very high pitch, loud, moderate-paced speech

Let’s take a moment to explore how we can shift that focus and identify some grounding techniques to help you feel more in control as you prepare for your presentation.

therapist: I can really feel how heavy this burden of judgment and anxiety is for you right now, especially since even the thought of trying something new feels daunting.
